summary: Republican Attorney General Alan Wilson leads Democratic state Rep. Jermaine Johnson for the open governor's seat, with an NPA poll reported by FITSNews showing Wilson ahead 51 to 41 among likely voters. Wilson is running on eliminating the income tax and lowering utility bills, while Johnson argues decades of one party control have left voters ready for change and backs Medicaid expansion.

issues.why: Wilson proposes eliminating the state income tax and cutting property taxes, the centerpiece of his closing ad.
Johnson notes South Carolina is one of 10 states that have not expanded Medicaid, while Wilson warns it could strain the budget.
Johnson backs a moratorium with community veto power, while Wilson prefers guardrails requiring data centers to generate their own power.
Both support regulated online sports betting, but Johnson would also allow casinos if voters approve and Wilson opposes them.
Johnson wants a statewide ban on Flock cameras over privacy, while Wilson calls them a valuable police tool.

storylines.title: Wilson's closing ad on income tax
storylines.what: Wilson launched his final statewide ad featuring his teenage children complaining about state income tax, promoting his plan to eliminate it.

storylines.title: Poll shows Wilson up double digits
storylines.what: An NPA poll of likely voters had Wilson at 51 percent and Johnson at 41, though undecided voters were splitting nearly evenly.

storylines.title: Early voting opens
storylines.what: Wilson campaigned in the Upstate while Johnson voted in Columbia and headed to the Grand Strand, criticizing corruption and backroom deals.

storylines.title: Wilson's fundraising edge
storylines.what: Wilson reported raising more than 2.5 million dollars last quarter compared with about 700,000 for Johnson.

storylines.title: Debate clash on crime and Medicaid
storylines.what: Wilson said he knows more about fighting fentanyl than Johnson will learn, and Johnson answered that Wilson has spent his career in statewide office while he worked on the ground.

storylines.title: Johnson pitches Medicaid expansion
storylines.what: Johnson called Medicaid expansion good economic policy, while Wilson pointed to North Carolina and warned of long term costs.

events.title: Eliminating the income tax
events.prompt: One campaign promises to eliminate the state income tax without new tax hikes. Voters ask what it would mean for schools and roads.

opts.label: Protect services
opts.say: Oppose elimination and argue it would starve schools and shift costs to working families.

opts.label: Targeted relief
opts.say: Cut taxes for working families and lower utility bills without ending the income tax.

opts.label: Go to zero
opts.say: Phase out the income tax entirely and let growth fill the gap.

events.title: Medicaid expansion
events.prompt: South Carolina is one of 10 states that has not expanded Medicaid. Rural hospitals want an answer.

opts.label: Expand now
opts.say: Expand Medicaid as good economic policy and bring federal dollars home.

opts.label: Study a waiver
opts.say: Explore a limited waiver with work rules and cost controls.

opts.label: Oppose expansion
opts.say: Reject expansion over long term costs that could crowd out teacher and police raises.

events.title: Data center moratorium
events.prompt: Communities are pushing back on data centers over power bills and land use. You must decide whether to pause them.

opts.label: Moratorium
opts.say: Pause new projects and give communities the final say.

opts.label: Guardrails
opts.say: Require data centers to generate their own power under state standards.

opts.label: Recruit them
opts.say: Keep recruiting data centers for jobs and investment with minimal new rules.

events.title: Casinos on the ballot
events.prompt: Lawmakers have stalled on gambling while neighboring states take the revenue. You are asked about sports betting and casinos.

opts.label: Betting and casinos
opts.say: Back online betting and let voters approve casinos.

opts.label: Online betting only
opts.say: Support regulated online sports betting but oppose casinos.

opts.label: No gambling
opts.say: Oppose any expansion of gambling in South Carolina.

ads.theme: His teenage children make the case for eliminating the state income tax.
